title: How to Implement D&O Coverage with the Best Startup Insurance Provider
summary: Learn what startup D&O insurance covers, how Side A, B and C work, and the steps to review a quote, bind coverage and meet board or investor requirements.
body_markdown:
1.


### Gather the requirements


Have your legal entity name, board composition, funding details, financial information and existing policy documents handy. Bring any requested limit or closing condition from the term sheet or board agreement. The insurer's application determines what else is needed.


2.


### Tell us the milestone and deadline


Explain whether you're closing a round, adding a director or renewing coverage. A funding stage gives useful context, but it doesn't automatically set the policy or change its limits.


3.


### Review the quote against the request


Check who is insured, the each-claim and aggregate limits, retentions, defense-cost treatment and exclusions. Review prior-acts or continuity terms, reporting requirements and any needed endorsements. Under Corgi's published D&O summary, defense costs reduce the amount available for other covered loss.


4.


### Confirm binding before sending proof


Complete any outstanding requirements and obtain confirmation of the effective date. Then provide the documents the investor or director requested. An application or quote alone doesn't mean the policy is active.


5.


### Review it as the company changes


D&O is claims-made, so follow the policy's claim-notice requirements and coordinate continuity before replacing it. Review board changes, financing and transaction plans when they arise and at renewal. Our


[switching guide](https://www.corgi.insure/blog/how-to-switch-business-insurance-providers) explains what to check before canceling an existing policy.
